feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring
entry.summary:
SWE-Bench ProMax is a multilingual code refactoring benchmark of 170 expert-curated instances across seven languages designed to address flaws and low complexity in existing coding agent benchmarks.

Why it matters: It provides an unsaturated, high-quality evaluation target that tests AI agents on complex, cross-file software refactoring without the noisy test suites of earlier benchmarks.

entry.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
entry.summary:
Macaron-V1 is an open agent-model family that uses recursive self-improvement and a Mixture-of-LoRA architecture to enable post-deployment continual learning.

Why it matters: It offers an open-source co-designed infrastructure that allows deployed models to continuously adapt and specialize without retraining the underlying base weights.

entry.title: Motif 3: Technical Report
entry.summary:
Motif 3 is a 314B parameter decoder-only MoE model utilizing Grouped Differential Latent Attention, activating 13.2B parameters across 384 routed experts to improve efficiency, stability, and broad domain performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how combining fine-grained MoE sparsity, architectural stabilization, and multi-teacher distillation can yield top-tier performance across reasoning, coding, and long-context tasks with reduced active compute per token.

entry.title: Agent Memory Distillation: Empowering Small LLM Agents with Hierarchical Teacher Memory
entry.summary:
Agent Memory Distillation (AMD) is a training-free framework that transfers structured, hierarchical teacher memory (Workflow, Subtask, and Function) from large LLMs to small 4B-8B student agents to boost tool-use performance.

Why it matters: AMD enables small language models (4B-8B parameters) to achieve high-tier tool-use capabilities without requiring expensive model retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains
entry.summary:
Sci-VBench is a new benchmark featuring 1,253 expert-annotated examples across 60 subjects to evaluate scientific reasoning and knowledge-grounded synthesis in video generation models.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that high perceptual quality in AI-generated video does not guarantee accurate modeling of real-world scientific and causal dynamics.

entry.title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution
entry.summary:
Ouroboros is a self-developing coding agent that recursively evolves its tools, prompts, context assembly, and core implementation through governed, reviewed commits.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that software agents can continuously self-improve their own codebase and performance on complex tasks without losing operational control or safety.

entry.title: DCAS: Decoupling CLI Agent Scaffolding to Internalize Planning across Scaffolds
entry.summary:
DCAS is an interception layer that decouples CLI agent scaffolding from backend models to train LLMs on planning-aware trajectories, mitigating fine-tuning-induced performance degradation across different evaluation scaffolds.

Why it matters: Decoupling planning from scaffold-specific artifacts allows models to internalize planning as a native capability, ensuring robust agent performance across diverse CLI environments.

entry.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SPOT improves on-policy distillation by using an acquisition-exploration-exploitation framework that sparsely probes teacher-proposed top-k candidates and calibrates distillation targets using verifier-scored student continuations.

Why it matters: SPOT enhances student model reasoning performance by ensuring distillation targets reflect downstream solution success rather than just local teacher token probabilities.

entry.title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour
entry.summary:
Fourteen language models (135M to 14B parameters) fine-tuned on the 10.7M-trial Psych-101 dataset show that 0.6B-1B parameter models match 70B baselines in-distribution, though larger models scale significantly better out-of-distribution.

Why it matters: Small cognitively fine-tuned models can efficiently serve as noise ceiling estimators for human psychological experiments without requiring massive 70B-parameter models for in-distribution tasks.

entry.title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching
entry.summary:
OasisKV decouples full KV-cache storage from HBM by using speculative decoding's lookahead tokens to predict and prefetch sparse, high-importance KV blocks from host/remote memory into HBM ahead of decode steps.

Why it matters: It enables memory-constrained inference systems to process significantly larger batch sizes and long-context workloads with up to double the throughput without losing generation accuracy.

entry.title: Relevant but Incomplete: Referential Dangling as a Paradigm-Level Failure Mode in Hard Prompt Compression
entry.summary:
Independent scoring in hard prompt compression causes referential dangling, where retained answer text loses the required entity context, degrading downstream model accuracy by up to 34 percentage points.

Why it matters: Hard prompt compression algorithms must be redesigned to ensure referential completeness alongside relevance, as even frontier language models cannot recover lost contextual dependencies.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection
entry.summary:
A new framework, FaceVid-Forensics-100K dataset, and multi-agent system improve deepfake video detection by analyzing four distinct forensic perspectives using open-source MLLMs.

Why it matters: This approach provides generalizable deepfake detection and interpretable forensic reasoning without relying on large closed-source multimodal language models.

entry.title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?
entry.summary:
Evo-Bench is the first benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' intrinsic capacity to autonomously evolve their own operating harnesses across Search, Office, and General agent domains.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate whether LLMs can self-optimize their execution frameworks, opening pathways for transferable, self-improving AI agent architectures.

entry.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement (CED) improves Vision-Language Model grounding by auditing whether model responses causally depend on specific visual evidence regions during Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training.

Why it matters: It enables Vision-Language Models to reduce hallucinations and dataset shortcuts by forcing causal reliance on visual context without incurring additional inference costs or requiring manual evidence annotations.

entry.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Steerling-8B, demonstrating that incorporating interpretability constraints directly into training pipelines allows interpretability to scale alongside language modeling capability without sacrificing performance.

Why it matters: It proves that models can be built inherently interpretable and steerable at scale without paying a performance penalty or requiring expensive compute-heavy post-hoc analysis.

entry.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement
entry.summary:
TIDE improves on-policy distillation by addressing teacher-student mismatch via bounded Hellinger shaping for student-excess tokens and analytic teacher top-K injection for student-deficit tokens.

Why it matters: TIDE stabilizes on-policy distillation under severe model mismatches, preventing degenerate generation loops and reducing formatting failures while shortening response lengths.

entry.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
SKALD uses on-policy self-distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher model conditioned on abstract skills into a question-only student model, overcoming zero-variance reward groups in reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It enables language models to internalize abstract reasoning skills directly into their weights, offering dense learning signals even when standard RL reward signals stall.

entry.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization (3PO), a parameter-space exploration framework for LLM reinforcement learning that samples diverse policy parameters to improve exploration beyond traditional action-space methods.

Why it matters: Parameter-space exploration provides a FLOP-efficient alternative to action-space methods, improving LLM reinforcement learning stability and task performance without additional computational overhead.

entry.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
SR-OPSD introduces a self-referenced on-policy self-distillation framework that stabilizes optimization by placing distillation targets via geometric interpolation and controlling projection geometry using Rényi divergence.

Why it matters: It improves optimization stability and performance across scientific, mathematical, and code generation tasks when tuning large language models with dense token-level feedback.

entry.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites
entry.summary:
A novel Matryoshka training framework stacks language sub-models into a single nested architecture, enabling end-to-end joint training, in-flight distillation, and parameter-efficient speculative decoding.

Why it matters: This architecture significantly cuts pre-training compute costs and enhances inference throughput without sacrificing model performance across size variants.

entry.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts
entry.summary:
MixFormer is a linear Transformer that combines a Mixture-of-Memory-Experts mechanism with Time-Aware Linear Attention to improve memory capacity and long-context sequence modeling.

Why it matters: By overcoming the memory capacity and input adaptivity limitations of standard SSMs, MixFormer offers a more computationally efficient backbone for long-context web infrastructure and generative tasks.

entry.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training
entry.summary:
WDL-OPD stabilizes on-policy distillation by co-training an anchor policy and an auxiliary policy using a mixture-constrained reverse KL loss against a frozen teacher.

Why it matters: Co-training two policies via a geometric mixture offers a targeted mechanism to prevent feedback loop instabilities and performance degradation in on-policy LLM distillation.

entry.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching
entry.summary:
Continuous depth batching (CDB) enables efficient depth-adaptive inference for looped LMs by scheduling at the loop-iteration level while handling non-looped boundary stages via separate priority queues.

Why it matters: CDB resolves batching inefficiencies in looped language models, enabling 1.5-1.9x higher offline throughput and up to 90% lower latency under dynamic serving loads.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Diagnostic of Rank Collapse in Post-Norm Decoder Transformers
entry.summary:
A two-stage analysis reveals that Post-Norm Transformer rank collapse stems from causal attention amplifying forward token similarity, which causes pre-norm residual norm growth that geometrically contracts backward gradients in RMSNorm layers.

Why it matters: Understanding the distinct forward amplification and backward gradient contraction mechanisms in Post-Norm architectures provides a clear diagnostic for why training dynamics fail to recover from rank collapse.

entry.title: Reducing Pretraining-Generation Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Prefix-Conditioned Diffusion (PCD) reduces pretraining-generation mismatch in diffusion language models by combining autoregressive prefix supervision with no-shift suffix denoising without changing the inference mode.

Why it matters: PCD narrows the performance gap between diffusion and autoregressive language models on continuation tasks without needing verifiers, extra decoders, or changes to inference.

entry.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
entry.summary:
SimWAM is an end-to-end autonomous driving model that uses video generation solely as a training signal via joint flow matching, enabling video-free, low-latency inference.

Why it matters: It eliminates the high computational latency of generating future video frames during inference while retaining the benefit of video dynamics priors for trajectory planning.

entry.title: Beyond Simply Environment Scaling: Designing Effective Environment Distributions for Multimodal Agent Learning
entry.summary:
Researchers show that simply scaling multimodal environments fails, introducing Ability-aware Environment Selection and Hierarchical Difficulty Curriculum to optimize environment diversity and difficulty structure for agent training.

Why it matters: It provides a structured methodology for constructing training environments, improving multimodal agent performance without relying on inefficient brute-force environment scaling.

entry.title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs
entry.summary:
A theoretical and empirical analysis reveals that multi-task SFT suffers from gradient norm-limited task conflicts, whereas RL enables stable task coexistence through variance-limited, sparse, near-orthogonal parameter updates.

Why it matters: Understanding RL's variance-limited gradient interference allows developers to decouple multi-task LLM training via Parallel-RL to improve training efficiency and flexibility without performance degradation.

entry.title: YOLO-PEFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on YOLO Family
entry.summary:
YOLO-PEFT introduces a structure-aware constraint-planning framework that evaluates detector-specific predicates to safely assign PEFT adapters or trigger an explicit refusal before fine-tuning real-time object detectors.

Why it matters: It automates adapter target selection and eliminates manual trial-and-error fine-tuning for real-time detectors while preventing catastrophic failures on incompatible architectures.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning
entry.summary:
AudioRubrics is a reinforcement learning framework that supervises audio reasoning by synthesizing and dynamically updating self-evolving, audio-grounded rubric rewards based on raw waveforms and model rollouts.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable method to train multimodal models on complex audio reasoning without relying on static, hand-crafted process rewards or easily gamed outcome-only feedback.

entry.title: StreamArena: Toward Continuous, Interactive, and Long-Horizon Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
StreamArena is a benchmark with 243 long-form videos averaging 88.8 minutes and 3,646 open-ended QA pairs for evaluating continuous, interactive, and long-horizon streaming video agents.

Why it matters: It provides a realistic, long-horizon evaluation framework and a decoupled dual-worker architecture to improve real-time responsiveness and historical context retention in continuous multimodal AI agents.

entry.title: Addressable Memory for Video World Models
entry.summary:
WorldTrace is a training-free memory framework for interactive video world models that maintains long-horizon visual persistence by assigning compressed Key-Value cache slots in-distribution virtual positions to prevent RoPE position-offset out-of-distribution failures.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon, visually persistent video generation in interactive world models without requiring expensive model retraining.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation
entry.summary:
The Uncertainty-Aware Navigation World Model (UA-NWM) improves aerial image-goal navigation by scoring trajectory-goal discrepancies using conditional out-of-distribution detection within a predicted uncertainty subspace.

Why it matters: It enables robust trajectory selection for UAVs in uncertain outdoor environments without incurring the high computational latency of sampling multiple future states.

entry.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
entry.summary:
Modular TTT formalizes test-time training as a directed acyclic graph of composable primitives, enabling systematic component ablation and the training of competitive 410M and 1.45B models.

Why it matters: It provides a unified, modular framework to systematically design and isolate TTT components, simplifying the search for efficient sequence modeling architectures.

entry.title: Skaling: Chinchilla's Exponents Meet Kaplan's Coupling
entry.summary:
The Skaling law introduces a generalized functional form that couples model capacity and training data via an interaction exponent, improving loss prediction accuracy at extreme data scales.

Why it matters: It enables highly accurate language model performance predictions from small-scale experiments, drastically reducing the compute required to plan optimal training budgets.

entry.title: Characterizing the Quality Profile of AI-Generated C++ in Production
entry.summary:
A year-long study of 3.52 million enterprise C++ code changes reveals that AI-generated code introduces distinct quality and performance overheads, but targeted taxonomy-informed feedback significantly mitigates these defects.

Why it matters: Unchecked AI-generated C++ increases production compute costs and review burdens, but automated, taxonomy-informed feedback loops can effectively restore code efficiency and quality at enterprise scale.

entry.title: When Privileged Guidance Misaligns: State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
entry.summary:
SMRC-SD prevents state-reference mismatch in multi-turn agent distillation by selectively routing privileged teacher guidance only to execution states that match the reference trajectory and conditioning teacher context on the current state.

Why it matters: It improves the reliability of privileged distillation for multi-turn RL agents by ensuring models are only supervised by reference trajectories that match their actual environment state.

entry.title: The Optimizer Is the Agent: Reasoning-Driven Search across Prompts, Programs, and ML Workflows
entry.summary:
ReASearch replaces hand-designed outer-loop optimization controllers with a single tool-using agent that internalizes search, failure diagnosis, memory, and budget allocation across prompts, programs, and ML workflows.

Why it matters: A single general reasoning agent can replace specialized optimization frameworks to improve prompts, software, and machine learning pipelines without requiring domain-specific search heuristics.

entry.title: Do AI Personas Grow? Analyzing and Benchmarking Personality Evolution in LLM Agents After Life Events
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated LLM agent personality evolution across 11 life events using Big Five traits, finding models mimic average human directional shifts but lack human-like magnitude, persona dispersion, and contextual variance.

Why it matters: Understanding the limitations of personality evolution in PC-Agents enables developers to build more realistic, psychologically grounded lifelong agents for social simulation and emotional support.

entry.title: PrivacyPeek: Auditing What LLM-Based Agents Acquire, Not Just What They Say
entry.summary:
PrivacyPeek is a new benchmark featuring 1,182 cases across 16 domains designed to audit acquisition-stage privacy leakage in LLM-based agents before information is disclosed in final responses or actions.

Why it matters: LLM agents routinely pulled sensitive, unnecessary data into their context windows, leaving systems vulnerable to simple follow-up probe attacks that existing output-focused benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Post-Grokking Collapse at the Representation-Readout Interface in Muon-Trained Transformers
entry.summary:
Muon-trained Transformers grok modular arithmetic faster than AdamW but suffer post-grokking generalization collapse caused by instability at the representation-readout interface, where Muon-updated parameters move 8.0 times faster per parameter post-solution.

Why it matters: Using the Muon optimizer on Transformer hidden layers accelerates initial grokking but introduces severe post-training instability that destroys generalization unless representation or readout layers are explicitly frozen.

entry.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Temperature Scaling: Bilevel Optimization for LLM Calibration
entry.summary:
A novel bilevel optimization framework trains LLM parameters directly by using a first-order approximation to optimize loss hyperparameters for predictive entropy maximization, surpassing domain-dependent post-hoc temperature scaling.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to maintain accurate confidence estimates and generalize better across unseen domains directly through training rather than fragile post-hoc adjustments.

entry.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
entry.summary:
Modular TTT formalizes test-time training inner learners as composable directed acyclic graphs, enabling systematic component ablation and automated composition of train-view and query-view execution rules.

Why it matters: It isolates the core algorithmic drivers of test-time training, preventing unnecessary Architectural complexity while enabling the automated synthesis and evaluation of new TTT variants.

entry.title: Skaling: Chinchilla's Exponents Meet Kaplan's Coupling
entry.summary:
The Skaling law introduces a unified scaling formulation that couples model capacity and training data via a single interaction exponent, eliminating systematic errors at data-scarce and overtraining extremes.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate language model performance predictions and compute budget allocation from small-scale training runs at a fraction of the traditional search cost.

entry.title: CreativeInstruct: Scalably Teaching LLMs to Balance Quality, Creativity, and Diversity
entry.summary:
CreativeInstruct is a scalable instruction-tuning method that uses [StartCreativity] special tokens to teach LLMs to balance post-trained generation quality with base-model-level output diversity and creativity.

Why it matters: It enables a single LLM to generate highly creative and diverse outputs without multi-model inference overhead, while also serving as a superior base checkpoint for downstream reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
entry.summary:
SkillProx is a self-evolving agent framework using proximal-gradient-inspired textual descent to refine, audit, and consolidate textual skills without updating LLM weights.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to automatically maintain efficient, high-performing textual skill libraries without suffering from performance regressions or uncontrolled skill bloating.

entry.title: Diffusion LLMs as Targets and Adversaries: Mechanistic Safety Exploits
entry.summary:
Researchers exposed mechanistic safety vulnerabilities in Diffusion LLMs, showing that safety alignment is sparse, transferable from autoregressive base models, and exploitable via neuron pruning and a low-cost offline jailbreak method.

Why it matters: The persistence of autoregressive safety neuron footprints in diffusion LLMs exposes them to low-cost mechanistic pruning attacks and enables highly efficient offline black-box jailbreaking against both open and proprietary models.

entry.title: CoBa: Cost-Effective Test-Time Scaling via Compute-Balanced Routing
entry.summary:
CoBa is a compute-balanced routing policy for test-time scaling that dynamically allocates inference compute between generation, cheap verification, and strong verification based on candidate uncertainty and value.

Why it matters: CoBa enables local reasoning systems to achieve state-of-the-art test-time scaling performance at more than half the computational cost of standard majority voting and weighted verification methods.

entry.title: PACE: Primitive-Aware Code Evolution for Automated Algorithm Design
entry.summary:
PACE introduces Executable Algorithmic Primitives (EAPs) to decouple local logic from whole programs, allowing LLM-based algorithm design to retain and transfer useful code components across program generations.

Why it matters: It prevents high-performing local code snippets from being discarded alongside subpar whole programs, increasing the efficiency and modularity of LLM-driven algorithm discovery.

entry.title: Geo-Spatial Concept Probing of Large Language Models: Abstraction, Compositionality, and Grounding
entry.summary:
A new geo-spatial benchmark isolates core properties of conceptual understanding—abstraction, compositionality, and grounding—using question answering to probe limitations across various LLM architectures, scale, and training regimes.

Why it matters: Identifying specific conceptual failures in spatial reasoning helps guide the design of future LLM architectures for better information access and structured knowledge management.

entry.title: From Economic Agents to Agentic Economies: A Systems Blueprint for Economic World Models
entry.summary:
This paper provides an implementation blueprint and six-level capability ladder for Economic World Models (EWMs) that generate macroeconomic dynamics through heterogeneous, adaptive AI agents interacting with evolving institutions.

Why it matters: EWMs provide a high-fidelity simulation environment to evaluate human economic policies and to train, test, and safely deploy autonomous AI decision-making agents.

entry.title: DataSpace: Benchmarking Data Agents for Verifiable Analytics over Heterogeneous Workspaces
entry.summary:
DataSpace is a new benchmark featuring 410 cross-language tasks across 15.01 GB of heterogeneous data artifacts to evaluate data agents' ability to generate verifiable tabular outputs from complex, multimodal organizational workspaces.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified, deterministic standard for measuring data agent accuracy when querying complex, cross-modal organizational environments.

entry.title: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains
entry.summary:
Researchers adapted the NVIDIA Nemotron stack for Modern Greek RAG applications across specialist domains, achieving significant retrieval and generation performance gains, and introduced HERA, a new Greek evaluation benchmark.

Why it matters: This work establishes effective open-source retrieval and grounded generation capabilities for Modern Greek across specialized legal, medical, energy, and financial domains where existing models fell short.

entry.title: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
entry.summary:
A deterministic, model-free compiler segments passively captured screen streams into typed activity frames, enabling 86x context compression and zero-token deterministic routine replay for computer-use agents.

Why it matters: This approach drastically reduces token costs and execution latencies for computer-use agents by replacing expensive LLM inference with deterministic, cached screen-activity memory.

entry.title: EffectLearner: World-Aware Object-Effect Reasoning for Real-World Video Object Removal
entry.summary:
EffectLearner combines a VLM-based Object-Effect Reasoner and a DiT-based Video Eraser to explicitly reason about and remove target objects and their associated physical effects from videos.

Why it matters: It enables accurate video object removal in real-world scenarios where objects create complex, dynamic, or spatially detached secondary effects like shadows and reflections.

entry.title: PaDoc: Layout-Grounded Parallel Decoding for Document Parsing
entry.summary:
PaDoc is a layout-grounded document parser that converts predicted page layouts into a branching structure to decode regional contents in parallel within a single Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM).

Why it matters: PaDoc eliminates the trade-off between full-page contextual accuracy and two-stage speed, significantly increasing parsing throughput and reducing latency without extra visual prefill overhead.

entry.title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models
entry.summary:
The KVAE family introduces open-source, continuous audio, image, and video tokenizers that match or surpass frontier open-source models in reconstruction and text-conditioned generation metrics.

Why it matters: Releasing these high-performing tokenizers alongside code and training details provides open-source foundations to improve latent diffusion model training speed and sample quality across modalities.

entry.title: MameLoshnLM: Yiddish Language Model and Evaluation Benchmark
entry.summary:
MameLoshnLM is the first open-source 8B-parameter Yiddish language model, created by continued pretraining of Llama 3.1 8B on a new curated corpus alongside a dedicated multi-task evaluation benchmark.

Why it matters: It establishes dedicated resources and a replication template to improve language modeling performance for digitally underrepresented low-resource languages with rich textual histories.

entry.title: Continual Learning in Transition
entry.summary:
A survey introduces a tri-axial framework analyzing the evolution of continual learning from parameter-centric model adaptation to system-level adaptation across three dimensions: When, How, and Where learning occurs.

Why it matters: It redefines continual learning by expanding focus beyond weight updates to system-level architectures and test-time adaptation.

entry.title: ContextMaster: Interactive Multi-Shot Video Creation via Fixed-Budget Sparse Context Routing
entry.summary:
ContextMaster is a unified model for interactive multi-shot video creation that manages expanding history via fixed-budget sparse context routing and ConstraintSink, achieving 16 FPS on a single GPU.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, interactive multi-shot video editing and generation with consistent history retention on a single GPU.

entry.title: MASS: Multiplayer World Models with Authoritative Shared State
entry.summary:
MAS disentangles world dynamics from view rendering by using a learned Logic Engine for an authoritative shared state and a separate Rendering Engine for independent camera view generation.

Why it matters: This architecture provides a scalable framework for simulating consistent, multi-agent virtual environments without relying on visual latents for state synchronization.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents
entry.summary:
This paper presents a systematic survey and object-centered taxonomy of self-evolving coding agents that continuously improve their models, memory, skills, tools, frameworks, and collaboration structures using execution feedback and repository context.

Why it matters: It establishes a conceptual foundation for building adaptive software engineering agents that learn and repair themselves from execution feedback rather than remaining static after deployment.

entry.title: Weights or Skills? A Survey of Robot-Learning Techniques: from Action-Predicting Weights to Robots that Write their Own Skills
entry.summary:
A new survey categorizes 77 robot-learning systems along a spectrum from action-predicting neural weights to code-based skills, detailing how code-as-policy methods achieve non-gradient self-improvement.

Why it matters: Understanding the architectural split between static policy weights and self-improving code skills guides the design of adaptable, verifiable, and open-ended robotic control systems.

entry.title: Task-Conditional Flow Matching for Balanced Multilingual Text Embedding Adaptation
entry.summary:
Task-Conditional Flow Matching (TCFM) adapts multilingual text embeddings by selectively applying Flow Matching to translation tasks while using task-aligned objectives for retrieval, classification, and pair-classification tasks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that applying task-specific optimization strategies rather than a single uniform objective prevents negative transfer and improves overall multilingual embedding performance.

entry.title: DRIFT: Derailing Denoising Trajectories of Flow-Matching VLAs with Adversarial Patch Attack
entry.summary:
DRIFT introduces a universal adversarial gripper patch that targets the multi-step denoising ODE of flow-matching VLAs, successfully breaking task execution in models like pi0 and pi0.5.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that flow-matching vision-language-action models share critical adversarial vulnerabilities with autoregressive models when attacks explicitly target their multi-step ODE trajectories.

entry.title: Continual Learning in Transition
entry.summary:
Continual learning is shifting from parameter-centric model adaptation to system-level adaptation, characterized across three dimensions: How, When, and Where learning occurs.

Why it matters: Expanding continual learning to external components and test-time updates allows systems to adapt dynamically without relying solely on computationally expensive retraining of static parameter weights.

entry.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
entry.summary:
SAGA is a parser-guided preference optimization framework that replaces human annotations with dependency-parser supervision to improve large language model grammatical alignment in low-resource Nordic languages.

Why it matters: SAGA demonstrates that automated dependency parsers can replace expensive human preference labels to effectively align language models in low-resource, morphologically rich languages.

entry.title: LLM Inference Under Bursty Workload Distribution: Modifying the WAIT Algorithm
entry.summary:
A lightweight extension to the WAIT scheduling algorithm performs online request intensity estimation from interarrival times, maintaining low latency and higher throughput under dynamic, bursty LLM workloads than existing baseline systems.

Why it matters: It enables LLM serving infrastructure to maintain low latency and maximize throughput under realistic, non-Poisson traffic bursts without needing pre-configured traffic models.

entry.title: Mapping Similarity Spaces across Embedding Models with Synthetic Query Probing
entry.summary:
Synthetic Query Probing maps similarity score distributions across different embedding models using query-chunk pairs, enabling score calibration without directly transforming vector spaces.

Why it matters: It enables threshold reuse and smoother model migration in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems without needing to re-index vector databases or recompute embeddings.

entry.title: Relay, Don't Route: Adaptive Population Handoff for Cost-Efficient LLM-Driven Evolution
entry.summary:
Relay is a training-free framework that uses an adaptive population handoff to shift LLM-driven evolutionary search budgets from individual calls to population-level transitions between cheap and strong models.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers token costs for LLM-based algorithm discovery and program search by structuring model usage around stateful population stages rather than per-query routing.

entry.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
A novel verifier-free breadth-depth refinement framework improves LLM reasoning by combining independent rollout sampling with iterative self-critique, self-correction, and majority voting.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that allocating test-time compute to repair local reasoning errors in candidate solutions is more effective than simply increasing sample volume or depending on external verifiers.

entry.title: Learning Context-Free Grammars for Grammar-Constrained Decoding via Declarative Agentic Programming with Guarantees
entry.summary:
Autogrammar automatically learns context-free grammars for esoteric DSLs from execution data using a language model framed as a Kripke structure governed by linear temporal logic constraints.

Why it matters: It enables reliable, syntactically valid code generation in low-resource domain-specific languages without requiring human experts to manually author complex context-free grammars.

entry.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
entry.summary:
READ replaces dense top-k vector retrieval with deterministic lexical search, structural navigation, and span reads via the Model Context Protocol, drastically outperforming embedding-based RAG on complex tabular documents.

Why it matters: Standard embedding-based RAG is structurally flawed for dense financial and regulatory documents, whereas deterministic, interpretable tool interfaces provide higher accuracy and replayable audit trails.

entry.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
entry.summary:
TS-RAG adapts retrieval-augmented generation to time series forecasting by using specialized reference tokens to fuse input sequences with retrieved similar historical patterns.

Why it matters: It enables time series models to leverage historical context and external data patterns via retrieval without requiring massive large language model architectures.

entry.title: What Current AI Benchmarks Leave Unmeasured: Modality, Search, Citations, and Implications (for Safety Evaluations)
entry.summary:
A study auditing ChatGPT's UI and API reveals that safety benchmarks like BBQ and SafetyBench are significantly affected by access modality, web search, and run-to-run inconsistency, which simple accuracy metrics fail to capture.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLMs solely via single-run API accuracy hides major behavioral instability, meaning standard benchmarks may misrepresent the real-world safety and reliability of deployed AI systems.

entry.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
entry.summary:
Ranking-based Reward Construction (RRC) bridges generative reward models and LLM reinforcement learning by deriving scalar rewards from relative preference rankings instead of absolute scoring paradigms.

Why it matters: RRC enables generative reward models to be effectively utilized as reward functions in reinforcement learning, improving model alignment on chat and reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that unconstrained diffusion LLMs fail at reasoning by committing final answers prematurely before completing chain-of-thought tokens, a pathology resolved using frontier-gated commitment order.

Why it matters: Enforcing sequential token commitment order is required to prevent reasoning collapse in diffusion LLMs without sacrificing their parallel decoding capabilities.

entry.title: BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians
entry.summary:
BaKron accelerates neural network quantization using Kronecker-factored Hessians by combining anti-diagonal parallelism with recursive divide-and-conquer processing.

Why it matters: It enables computationally efficient neural network quantization that leverages rich two-sided curvature information without exceeding the scaling limits of standard GPTQ approaches.

entry.title: The Illusion of Visual Tool-Use: A Causal Audit of Thinking with Images
entry.summary:
A causal audit of multimodal LLM visual tool-use reveals that active visual operations like crop-and-zoom often lack causal effect on final answers despite aggregate accuracy gains.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that visual tool-use in multimodal LLMs frequently incurs high token costs and extra compute without causally driving the model's reasoning or final output.

entry.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
EnvACE is an agentic reinforcement learning method that replaces external environment interactions during training with joint, end-to-end world rehearsal of both tool calls and environment responses.

Why it matters: It removes the need for costly external simulators or real executable environments during LLM agent RL training by internalizing environment dynamics directly into the model.

entry.title: Visual Grounding in Zero-Shot Vision-Language Control
entry.summary:
A systematic input-ablation study of 32,874 VLM controller calls reveals widespread grounding failures in direct zero-shot visual control, while demonstrating that VLMs function reliably as modular hazard assistants when paired with symmetry-consensus guardians.

Why it matters: Current vision-language models are unsuitable as monolithic zero-shot end-to-end controllers, but can safely serve as bounded, selective hazard assistants within modular control architectures.

entry.title: Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
The Globalized Skill Evolution (GSE) framework continuously improves LLM coding agents by co-evolving inter-skill relationships in a graph, consolidating cluster-based skills, and using replay verification to prevent overfitting.

Why it matters: GSE enables LLM software engineering agents to continuously self-improve and generalize across complex tasks without costly full model retraining.

entry.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents
entry.summary:
Contextual Information Policy Optimization (CIPO) is a novel reinforcement learning framework that provides dense, turn-level rewards to align search agent reasoning actions directly with retrieved external evidence without relying on extra reward models.

Why it matters: CIPO improves search agent reliability and efficiency on knowledge-intensive tasks by forcing agents to actively base and revise their multi-step reasoning on retrieved evidence rather than internal guesses.

entry.title: Beyond Sequence Order: Syntax-Informed Positional Embeddings for Transformers
entry.summary:
SiPE introduces syntax-informed positional embeddings that inject a lightweight dependency parse prior into absolute, relative, and rotary Transformers without altering self-attention architecture or degrading perplexity.

Why it matters: It provides a method to incorporate structural language priors into Transformers that enhances downstream task performance and syntactic accuracy while simultaneously improving language model perplexity.

entry.title: When History Lies: Evaluating and Improving Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce a paired benchmark and a teacher-student prefix-distillation method to evaluate and mitigate LLM agent tool-calling failures caused by misleading, non-authoritative multi-turn execution histories.

Why it matters: It establishes history reliability as a key bottleneck in multi-turn tool use and provides a scalable distillation approach to prevent agents from using stale or corrupted dialogue context.

entry.title: HERALD: Counterfactual Audits and Minimal Repairs for Proof-of-Retrieval Rewards
entry.summary:
HERALD introduces offline counterfactual audits for search-agent rewards, identifying a citation-laundering vulnerability and proving that a targeted penalty on unretrieved cited passages ($L$) serves as an inclusion-minimal repair.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how counterfactual auditing can detect and fix subtle reward-hacking vulnerabilities in search-agent reward functions without degrading general model performance.

entry.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
AgentOPSD introduces a critic-free, recursive self-distillation method that aggregates token-level log-probability gaps into turn-level credit using Bayesian belief updates in log-odds space for agentic RL.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient way to resolve credit assignment in long-horizon agent tasks without the memory overhead or training instability of a separate critic model.

entry.title: How Far Do Simple Transformations Translate Across Text Embedding Models?
entry.summary:
A study evaluating lightweight linear transformations across nine heterogeneous text embedding models reveals that simple mappings fail to universally translate semantic representations, contradicting the broad latent universality hypothesis.

Why it matters: AI-to-AI latent communication cannot rely solely on simple linear transformations to bridge diverse text embedding spaces without full decoding.

entry.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
entry.summary:
An empirical evaluation of 14 LLMs on BFCL v4 demonstrates that programmatic tool calling using typed Python stubs matches or outperforms native JSON tool calling, with improvements up to 10.6% on the GPT-5.6 family.

Why it matters: Replacing JSON tool calls with programmatic Python scripts offers a more robust, scalable mechanism for agentic tool use without requiring changes to underlying model capabilities.

entry.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
entry.summary:
RP-OPSD improves cross-lingual LLM reasoning transfer by using distributional shifts between teacher views to concentrate on-policy self-distillation on critical reasoning pivots rather than surface text.

Why it matters: It enables more effective cross-lingual reasoning transfer in LLMs by focusing compute and supervision on key decision points rather than language-specific surface text.

entry.title: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
entry.summary:
Evaluation of six observation modes across eight web agent setups shows that task-level representation routing fails to outperform a single fixed mode due to run-to-run noise and sparse supervision signals on weaker agents.

Why it matters: Until web agents achieve higher baseline success rates to generate sufficient training labels, practitioners should default to a single optimal observation mode rather than complex task-level routing pipelines.

entry.title: Causal Episodic Memory for Feedback-Driven Agent Repair
entry.summary:
MERIT is a training-free LLM agent that improves Text-to-SQL error repair by maintaining an online dual-polarity memory of oracle-verified corrections and failed attempts from past episodes.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that agents can incrementally improve code and SQL generation performance across successive query tasks using lightweight, episodic memory without costly parameter updates.

entry.title: Decomposed Entailment for Factuality Checking and Hallucination Detection
entry.summary:
HallDetect is a lightweight, black-box hallucination detection framework that decomposes text into atomic claims and evaluates them against multi-scale source chunks using a compact encoder-based entailment model and asymmetric score aggregation.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, resource-efficient, and interpretable hallucination detection across diverse source-grounded generation tasks on consumer-grade hardware.

entry.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify an irreversible skill-contamination phase transition in self-evolving LLM agents and introduce Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG), a pre-commit gating framework that prevents defective skills from entering the decision context.

Why it matters: Preventing defective skills prior to integration is essential for LLM agents, as post-hoc skill deletion fails to reverse reasoning flaws inherited by downstream distilled skills.

entry.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning
entry.summary:
On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD2) uses the probability gap between a post-trained teacher and its base model to outperform standard On-Policy Distillation in multilingual math reasoning across English, Korean, and Japanese.

Why it matters: It provides a more effective post-training distillation method that strengthens non-English mathematical reasoning without causing output language drift.

entry.title: Task-Conditional Flow Matching for Balanced Multilingual Text Embedding Adaptation
entry.summary:
Task-Conditional Flow Matching (TCFM) selectively applies Flow Matching to translation tasks while using task-aligned objectives for retrieval, classification, and pair-classification to improve multilingual embedding adaptation.

Why it matters: TCFM demonstrates that tailoring training objectives to specific task dynamics rather than using a single uniform objective significantly improves multilingual text embedding quality and generalization.

entry.title: GROM: Gradient-Free Rapid One-Shot Machine Unlearning
entry.summary:
GROM introduces a gradient-free, one-shot machine unlearning method that uses a ridge-regularized least-squares closed-form analytical update to permanently remove targeted LLM knowledge in seconds.

Why it matters: It provides an orders-of-magnitude faster unlearning process that securely erases sensitive LLM data without susceptibility to quantization-based knowledge recovery attacks.

entry.title: Once a Response, Always a Response: Detecting LLM-generated Text via Latent Prompt Restoration
entry.summary:
EchoPrompt is a training-free, zero-shot LLM-generated text detector that quantifies latent prompt dependency by measuring likelihood gain from a generic assistant-response context restored via an instruction-tuned model and calibrated against a base model.

Why it matters: By explicitly modeling the instruction-following generation mechanism rather than relying solely on statistical probability discrepancies, EchoPrompt improves zero-shot detection robustness against AI-generated text risks.

entry.title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation
entry.summary:
A novel method mitigates LLM-as-a-Judge scoring bias by measuring an LLM's task-specific latent number bias via random number generation and rectifying token generation probabilities accordingly.

Why it matters: It provides a task-specific calibration technique to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-based automated evaluation systems without requiring reference texts.

entry.title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs
entry.summary:
A novel three-stream detector evaluates LLM reasoning accuracy by combining residual-stream motion (displacements) with state context (coarse region via vector quantization and fine direction via normalized multi-layer states) rather than relying on static states or decontextualized trajectories alone.

Why it matters: It enables more reliable identification of LLM reasoning errors and factual hallucinations across diverse tasks without requiring full-state probing or task-specific retraining.
